global_rules.source_affordance: Every chart must expose source_id, title, publisher, URL, locator, access date, baseline, unit, confidence, and caveats.
global_rules.uncertainty: Render assessed ranges as bands or error bars; never hide them only in a tooltip.
global_rules.nulls: Render unavailable values as gaps; never replace null with zero or interpolate without a source-authorized method.
global_rules.precision: Do not display more precision than the source.
global_rules.baseline: Temperature and sea-level baselines must be visible adjacent to the axis or subtitle.
global_rules.language: Label observations, causal attribution, projections, scenarios, and correlations distinctly.

charts.title: How human emissions warm the climate
charts.annotation: Natural drivers and internal variability affect individual years but do not explain the multi-decadal warming trend.

charts.title: Greenhouse gases, forcing, and temperature
constraints: Do not put unlike units on an unlabeled dual axis.
Preserve each temperature series' native baseline or explicitly rebase both using a documented overlap method.
charts.annotation: Co-movement is descriptive; causal attribution comes from physics and formal forcing experiments.

charts.title: Why a high trend correlation is not the attribution test
charts.annotation: Both concentration and temperature trend upward; first differences are dominated by short-term variability and measurement timing.

charts.title: What caused observed warming
constraints: Other human drivers must be drawn as cooling, not missing warming.
Retain likelihood ranges.

charts.title: Cumulative carbon dioxide commits warming
constraints: The observed cumulative series is context; do not claim it exactly reproduces the IPCC attribution estimate.
Do not apply TCRE to CO2e or annual emissions.

charts.title: Assessed warming under five emissions pathways
constraints: Show 20-year assessment periods, not invented annual points.
Do not label scenarios as forecasts or probabilities.

charts.title: Risks compound with every increment of warming
constraints: Separate units into panels.
Do not connect missing warming levels.
Display confidence and geography.

charts.title: Tropical-cyclone risk: intensity and rainfall, not a simple count
charts.annotation: Rising sea level independently raises coastal inundation.

charts.title: Species at very high extinction risk
constraints: Label as modeled risk, not observed extinction.
Pair with the five IPBES direct drivers.

charts.title: Major-crop yield sensitivity to warming
constraints: Never place the two groups on one numeric scale without distinct units.
Expose CO2-fertilization and adaptation assumptions.
Do not relabel yield as food security.

charts.title: Freshwater risk changes by place, season, and demand
constraints: Map only with spatial source data; current global values are not mappable.
Keep low-confidence labels adjacent to 3-billion and 4-billion estimates.
Do not use global freshwater loss as a numeric metric.

charts.title: Sea level: observed acceleration and future commitment
constraints: Visually break historical and projection periods.
State the 1995-2014 projection baseline.
Do not show global mean as a local forecast.
charts.future_localization_dependency: regional relative sea-level projections with vertical land motion

charts.title: Displacement observations and internal-migration scenarios
constraints: Never sum observed displacement flows with modeled migration stocks.
Label Groundswell as internal and scenario-based.
Do not use climate refugee as a chart category.
